title: ASML: The Machine That Makes the World's Most Advanced Chips
description: Your smartphone contains billions of microscopic switches. But who builds the machine that prints them? This video explains how chips are made with photolithography, why engineers kept chasing shorter wavelengths of light, how immersion lithography and multiple patterning stretched older technology, and how ASML's EUV machines create extreme ultraviolet light by firing lasers at tiny droplets of molten tin up to 50,000 times every second. See why glass lenses cannot be used, how multilayer mirrors from ZEISS and lasers from TRUMPF fit in, why the whole system runs in a vacuum, and why no other company has built a commercial equivalent. Then learn what High-NA EUV is, how fabless companies, foundries like TSMC and integrated device manufacturers fit together, and why older DUV technology still matters.
